corrected_value.title: Alcohol use disorder symptoms are associated with greater relative value ascribed to alcohol, but not greater discounting of costs imposed on alcohol.

decisions.location: Independent primary-source passage 0059_P_explicit_relation; complete current Methods/Results/Discussion and verified original context0158
decisions.quote: Our behavioral findings partially replicate previous results, showing that choice preference for alcohol was affected by the relative value of the alternative reward (Hogarth & Hardy,  2018 ; Karlsson et al.,  2024 ). In both groups, alcohol choice increased as alcohol was associated with more points compared to snack. Thus, alcohol was less favored when it was associated to the cost of losing the more valuable alternative reward, indicating similar sensitivity to cost in both groups.
decisions.reason: The current new-sample scanner study explicitly compares its own relative-value alcohol-choice and AUDIT-choice findings with BOTH Hogarth/Hardy2018 and Karlsson2024, stating the prior AUDIT result came from two task versions and laboratories. This is direct retesting and own-result comparison, beyond mere task adaptation. The complete2018primary report identifies127Exeter student drinkers and the original alcohol-versus-chocolate relative-value/AUDIT findings. Current Methods power from that original and Results analyze the corresponding behavioral components. Existing988 represents the different Karlsson investigation; the current two-laboratory account positively distinguishes the prior reports, so the2018finding is genuinely absent. No crossed-delay outcome, original-cohort overlap or novel neural claim is inferred. Outcome is not requested. The final raw rationale contains unsupported original statistics: the actual2018relative-magnitude test is F(4,500)=20.79, AUDIT main effect F(1,125)=11.75/r=.29, and opportunity interaction F(4,500)=1.25,p=.289, rather than the final reply values. This independent source decision preserves that error and does not adopt it.
